summary: Add an optional `styles.toggle` section to ZestGlobalConfig (the existing ZestButtonConfigProvider/context), and an optional `style` field on ToggleOptions for per-button overrides. Settings are organised by button kind (`toggle` only for now) as { base state looks, `light`/`dark` theme looks, `variants.<ZestVariant>`, `sizes.<ZestSize>` }, each holding per-state looks (off, on, hoverOff, hoverOn, focus, disabled, busy) as maps of CSS property name -> value. A pure compile step sanitises the settings (R8, security NFR: property names must match /^[a-zA-Z-]+$/ or be a known custom key; values must be strings/numbers with no `;`, `{`, `}`, `<`, `url(`/`expression(`/`@import`/comment tokens, otherwise the single property is dropped) and flattens them, for the button's resolved theme, variant and size, using the precedence all-toggles < size < variant < provider theme < per-button (R4, R5, R6), into declarations per state. The compiled declarations are emitted once as one CSS rule per state under a generated class/attribute id (`[data-zest-toggle-style="<id>"]`, selector specificity raised by repeating the attribute so it beats the library's own `.solid.toggleOn:hover:not(:disabled)` rules without `!important`), so pseudo-states (hover, focus-visible, disabled, busy) work, which inline styles cannot do. Rules go into one shared, ref-counted <style> element in document.head (inserted in an effect, so Next.js server rendering and React 18/19 are unaffected; the button just gets the data attribute). Compilation is memoised per settings object (WeakMap keyed on the provider's `styles.toggle` and on the per-button `style` object) and per (theme, variant, size) key, and rule insertion is deduplicated by id, so 100 toggles under one provider do the work once, an unchanged config object does no recompute, and unmounting releases the ref count and removes unused rules. No new dependencies, no timers, no listeners. The library's own CSS is untouched (no new px), the focus indicator stays unless the developer sets a `focus` look, and aria-pressed/keyboard/check mark logic is not changed. Only the data attribute (and `data-zest-toggle-check` on the already aria-hidden check svg for check colour/size) is added to the toggle render path. Public surface grows additively through the existing `export *` lines in UI/index.ts; version gets a minor bump; docs are updated in documentation/ and README.
